job_title: Senior Perception AI Engineer - Autonomous Vehicles
job_description: Self-driving cars need to understand the road ahead in real time, even without a prior map. Our team builds the online mapping system that turns raw data from multiple sensors into an accurate, continuously updated 3D model of the driving environment. This model captures lanes, road boundaries, crosswalks, intersection layouts, and traffic control information to support decisions across the autonomous driving system. You’ll write the models, write the C++, and ship both into vehicles on the road, running on NVIDIA DRIVE Orin and Thor. The tasks you perform will be tested at scale, on real cars, with real safety requirements. NVIDIA’s autonomous driving stack spans the full range of automation, and online mapping is a core component across it, so your work will reach L2++, L3, and L4 systems. The role spans two subject areas, and we want someone who enjoys both: Learned mapping involves training DNNs to predict map elements directly from visual sensors, laser scanning, and radar. This includes owning the GT story and collaborating with partners to provide the vital data. Geometry and C++ engineering: building the post-processing that turns network outputs into stable, consistent, production-ready map elements. What you’ll be doing: Design, train, and improve PyTorch models that predict online map elements (lanes, road boundaries, crosswalks, road markings, topology) from camera, LiDAR, and/or radar, using BEV and vectorized-map representations. Solve the hardest scenes: model intersection topology (connectivity between incoming and outgoing lanes, turn paths, merges and splits) and traffic light understanding (detection, state, and association of each light to the lanes it controls). Write production C++ for geometry-based post-processing: curve and surface fitting, association, multi-frame fusion and tracking, topology reasoning, and consistency checks on DNN outputs. Apply multi-view geometry, calibration, coordinate transforms, and sensor fusion to produce 3D maps that stay accurate and stable over time. Optimize and deploy models alongside algorithms on NVIDIA DRIVE Orin and Thor under real-time and safety constraints, and get them running in vehicles. Lead the narrative around GT and the data loop by planning datasets and defining GT and labeling requirements. Work with labeling, data, and tooling partners to produce high-quality GT. Mine data, choose metrics, and analyze failure cases to drive improvements. Define critical metrics and build evaluation tooling to measure quality gains against large-scale real-world data. Partner with perception, localization, planning, and infrastructure teams to integrate online mapping into the full AV stack, across L2++, L3, and L4 programs. Contribute to technical direction and architecture decisions across the learned and geometric components of the mapping system. What we need to see: MS or PhD or equivalent experience in Computer Science, Electrical Engineering, Robotics, or a related field, or equivalent experience 5+ years of industry or research experience in autonomous driving, robotics, or computer vision. Strong foundation in 3D geometry: camera models, projective geometry, coordinate transforms, optimization, and curve/surface fitting. Strong C++ skills, with a track record of designing and shipping production-quality algorithm code that is fast, reliable, and maintainable. Hands-on experience training deep neural networks in PyTorch, including model design, training pipelines, debugging, and performance analysis. Experience with data-driven development: building datasets, defining labels and GT, choosing metrics, and improving models by analyzing failures.
